Cache Configuration

1. Key Configuration Parameters
ParameterDescriptionDefault
nameCache name (must be unique)None (required)
cacheModePARTITIONED, REPLICATED, or LOCALPARTITIONED
atomicityModeATOMIC or TRANSACTIONALATOMIC
backupsNumber of backup copies (partitioned mode)0
writeSynchronizationModeFULL_SYNC, FULL_ASYNC, or PRIMARY_SYNCPRIMARY_SYNC
rebalanceModeSYNC, ASYNC, or NONEASYNC
readFromBackupRead from local backup if availabletrue
partitionLossPolicyBehavior when partitions are lostIGNORE
eagerTtlEagerly remove expired entriestrue
2. Write Synchronization Modes
  • FULL_SYNC — the client waits until the write is confirmed by the primary node AND all backup nodes; safest but slowest;
  • PRIMARY_SYNC (default) — the client waits until the primary node confirms; backups are updated asynchronously; good balance of safety and performance;
  • FULL_ASYNC — the client does not wait at all; fastest but risk of data loss on failure;
3. Full Configuration Example
  • CacheConfiguration<Integer, Person> cacheCfg = new CacheConfiguration<>("PersonCache");

cacheCfg.setCacheMode(CacheMode.PARTITIONED);
cacheCfg.setAtomicityMode(CacheAtomicityMode.TRANSACTIONAL);
cacheCfg.setBackups(2);
cacheCfg.setWriteSynchronizationMode(CacheWriteSynchronizationMode.FULL_SYNC);
cacheCfg.setRebalanceMode(CacheRebalanceMode.SYNC);
cacheCfg.setReadFromBackup(true);
cacheCfg.setPartitionLossPolicy(PartitionLossPolicy.READ_ONLY_SAFE);

IgniteConfiguration igniteCfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
igniteCfg.setCacheConfiguration(cacheCfg);

Ignite ignite = Ignition.start(igniteCfg);
4. Cache Templates
  • A cache template is a pre-registered CacheConfiguration that can be used as a basis for creating new caches;
  • Useful when thin clients or SQL need to create caches with specific settings; 
    CacheConfiguration template = new CacheConfiguration("myTemplate*");
template.setBackups(2);
template.setCacheMode(CacheMode.PARTITIONED);
ignite.addCacheConfiguration(template);

// Later, create a cache from the template
CREATE TABLE Person (...) WITH "template=myTemplate";
  • Template names must end with * when registered via XML;
5. Immutability After Creation
  • Once a cache is created, most configuration parameters cannot be changed;
  • To change configuration, you must destroy the cache and recreate it;
  • Some parameters (like memory policy size) can be adjusted at the cluster level;
